sources.entry: Tingo - Open-source meeting notes app that records any call, transcribes it and tells speakers apart on device, and writes minutes whose every point links back to the original audio, using the LLM you choose. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/tancheng33/tingo) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Tingo is an open-source, on-device meeting notes app for Mac (Apple Silicon) that records system audio and microphone, transcribes Chinese and English speech locally, separates speakers, and writes minutes with timestamped links back to the original audio.
summary.what_it_does: Records system audio (for example from Tencent Meeting, Feishu, or Zoom) and the local microphone, then transcribes the audio on the user's machine using FunASR-based models such as Paraformer-large, SenseVoice, or Fun-ASR-Nano. It separates speakers by voiceprint and can ask an LLM to guess speaker names from context. Meeting minutes are generated by an OpenAI-compatible LLM the user chooses, including DeepSeek, Qwen, or local Ollama, with issues, decisions, action items with owners and deadlines, and risks. Each point carries a timestamp that jumps to the audio, and a fishbone diagram for cause analysis checks each branch against the transcript. Outputs include PDF, Word, SRT subtitles, Obsidian notes, Markdown, and pushes to Feishu, DingTalk, or WeCom group bots. The README also describes a command-line version (tingo) for scripted or batch processing of recordings.
use_cases: record and transcribe online meetings locally
generate meeting minutes with action items
keep meeting audio off the cloud
export meeting notes to Word, PDF, or Obsidian
batch process existing meeting recordings from the command line
how_to_run: uv tool install git+ # or pipx install git+… (command-line version, Python 3.11+)
tingo record -t 周会 -w "林舟,注册转化"
Desktop app: download Tingo_x.y.z_aarch64.dmg from GitHub Releases and drag it into Applications
stack: FunASR (Paraformer, VAD, punctuation, CAM++ speaker model)
notable: Audio stays on the device: recognition and speaker separation run locally, and Ollama allows fully offline minutes generation
Every minutes item has a timestamp that links back to the original spoken words; fishbone diagram branches are checked against the transcript and unsupported ones are flagged
Captures system audio directly without a virtual sound driver such as BlackHole, according to the README
Desktop app is about 13 MB, built with Tauri and Rust, with no Python or ffmpeg needed
Built for Chinese meetings, with time phrases like 'next Wednesday' converted to actual dates, plus a glossary of names and terms
caveats: Desktop app supports only Apple Silicon Macs on macOS 13+, and system audio capture requires macOS 15+; Windows support is on the roadmap only
Command-line version on Linux can record only the microphone; Windows users must record with the meeting software and import the file

Speaker separation can misassign speakers when people talk over each other or sound similar; external-speaker echo is handled by ducking the mic rather than true echo cancellation, and wearing headphones works best
Initial setup downloads a model of about 330 MB; minutes generation needs an LLM API key unless a local Ollama model is used
